historical.text: Hill fort in the Sahyadri range south-west of Pune, also called Prachandagad. Its acquisition is traditionally treated as Shivaji's first major fort gain, usually dated c. 1646-47. The exact date and whether it fell by force or by arrangement vary by account.
sources: Sarkar, Jadunath. Shivaji and His Times

rajgad.name: Rajgad

historical.text: Fort developed on Murumbdev hill near Torna. Accounts describe it as an early headquarters of Shivaji before Raigad became the principal seat; dates of construction and use differ between sources.
sources: Sarkar, Jadunath. Shivaji and His Times
Mehendale, Gajanan B. Shivaji: His Life and Times

rajgad.gameplay_note: Walls start low (30) to represent a fort still being built. This is a gameplay representation.

historical.text: Fort south-west of Pune, known as Kondana before the later name Sinhagad. Accounts differ on when Shivaji first held it and on a traditional story that it was returned to Adil Shahi control as part of the arrangement for his father Shahaji's release around 1649.
sources: Sarkar, Jadunath. Shivaji and His Times

historical.text: Major hill fort south-east of Pune. Shivaji's possession from about 1648 is traditional; some accounts describe a dispute within the family holding the fort as the opening he used. Details and sequence are not agreed.
sources: Sarkar, Jadunath. Shivaji and His Times
Mehendale, Gajanan B. Shivaji: His Life and Times

chakan.name: Chakan

historical.text: Small ground fort north of Pune. It is best known for the 1660 siege by Mughal forces, which is outside this scenario's period. Its holder in 1646-1649 is uncertain, so its starting owner here is a gameplay assumption.
sources: Sarkar, Jadunath. Shivaji and His Times

chakan.gameplay_note: Ground fort: weak walls, but cheap to take and a useful first target.
